blocks.content: ImagePullBackOff means kubelet cannot pull the image a Pod specifies, following the exact same retry-with-backoff pattern covered in the CrashLoopBackOff topic, just triggered by a failed pull instead of a crash.
1. The Image Simply Cannot Be Pulled
blocks.text: 1. The Image Simply Cannot Be Pulled

blocks.content: Before a container can even start, kubelet has to successfully pull its image, when that pull genuinely fails, the container never gets a chance to run at all.

blocks.alt: A failure before the container ever even gets a chance to start

blocks.content: 2. A Typo in the Image Name or Tag
blocks.text: 2. A Typo in the Image Name or Tag

blocks.content: This is a genuinely common, easy mistake, a misspelled image name, or a tag that does not actually exist, causes the registry to correctly report that nothing matching was found.

blocks.alt: A simple typo, a surprisingly common real-world cause

blocks.content: This connects directly to the dockerconfigjson Secret type covered in the Configuration module, if the image lives in a private registry and the Pod does not reference the right imagePullSecrets, kubelet has no way to authenticate, and the pull fails.

blocks.alt: The exact Secret type and imagePullSecrets mechanism covered in the Configuration module

spec:
  imagePullSecrets:
    - name: registry-creds
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: myregistry.com/team/myapp:1.0

blocks.content: 4. The Image Genuinely Does Not Exist
blocks.text: 4. The Image Genuinely Does Not Exist

blocks.content: Sometimes the image tag simply was never pushed, or was later deleted from the registry, exactly the kind of issue covered conceptually back in the Docker Registry module, worth verifying directly rather than assuming.

blocks.alt: A real possibility worth verifying directly, not just assuming a typo

blocks.content: The status genuinely follows the same shape as CrashLoopBackOff, an initial ErrImagePull, then repeated retries with increasing delay under ImagePullBackOff, exactly the same underlying backoff mechanism, applied here.

blocks.alt: The exact same backoff mechanism covered for crashing containers, applied to failed pulls

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: ImagePullBackOff means kubelet cannot successfully pull the specified image, a typo, missing registry credentials, or a genuinely missing image are the common causes.
It follows the same retry-with-backoff pattern as CrashLoopBackOff, ErrImagePull first, then repeated, increasingly delayed retries.
